**Internet Digital Ark Project**

**Task Brief Update Log**

Purpose: Record the timestamp, content, and practical implications of each task brief update so that all contributors can clearly trace how the project requirements and discovery methods evolve.

# Update Record

**Timestamp:** 2026-08-15 15:39:36 (UTC+8)

**Related document:** Internet_Digital_Ark_Project_0815_Update.docx

**Update topic:** Expanding domain discovery through existing historical and academic data sources

## Changes in This Update

Existing academic datasets, historical web research archives, link lists, and link graphs covering 1996-2001 are now explicitly recognized as sources for discovering additional historical domains.

The early-web link-list dataset from the University of Minnesota Data Repository (UMN DRUM) has been added as a validated example. It demonstrates that existing academic archives with traceable year evidence can support large-scale extraction and verification of historical domains.

Contributors are encouraged to search more broadly across university and research repositories, DOI dataset platforms, digital libraries, paper supplements, replication packages, historical web research projects, and other public data sources to continue expanding the unknown-domain list.

## Direction and Scope

Extracting domains from existing historical and academic archives is a high-value direction confirmed by this update, but it is not the only direction. Future work should remain open-ended and innovative, continuing to identify both similar and entirely new domain-discovery methods.
